entry.title: /toʊ/
entry.content:
Intro

This episodic statement explores the territory of concept and structure, reflecting an artist’s recognition of crisis from diverse perspectives. Having lived as a minority in Iran, later as an immigrant in Russia and Germany, and through encounters with various people, the artist aims to achieve a broad, universal observation. By empathizing and putting themselves in others’ shoes, the artist seeks to understand the challenges of different pathways, thereby gaining deeper meaning through alternative viewpoints. Through this process, the following question becomes recognized as a unified point to share with others.

What is the Current Crisis?

Skipping a long list of what can be defined as a crisis and picking only one topic, freedom is the most likely choice. The answer to the question ‘Why?’ could be because everything starts from the point where we assume a boundary for the ‘individual’, both in terms of hypothesis and reality.

The limitation of freedom applies to every individual, with extreme cases often related to nationality, gender, race, sex, and other factors.

Earlier, I mentioned a portion of the limitations on freedom that affect everyone. While extreme cases might not be the only target, these limitations still impact already persecuted minorities. These limitations can lead to forced persecutions that threaten the very existence of a large number of individuals.

As a result of these limitations, identity crisis has become a topic frequently used for various purposes, such as in social media, politics, philosophy, art, science, and other criteria of criticism. Dealing with identity crises as individuals not only leads to a loss of identity but also results in forgetting the conversation with oneself. In society, this mostly appears as manipulated voices and remains as a blind imitation of given labels coming from immoral and outdated sources.

Discovery and Development of the Manipulation from Scratch

From the first instance that the human voice comes into existence, an additional instrument can be directly mounted on the larynx to manipulate the sound of speech from scratch. The exploration began with the discovery of the first version during an extended sound rehearsal session on the piano with Lydia Krifka-Dobes in Fall 2022.

I was thinking aloud when, accidentally, an electric massager made contact with my throat. The resulting sound was so interesting that we couldn’t resist listening to it a second time. This experience created a need to explore the combination of the human voice and transducer speakers on the throat in multiple vocal pieces of music, and that exploration is still in progress.

Technical Approach

When there are two sounds from two different sources with slightly different frequencies, they create a phenomenon known in physics as beats. This special kind of beating, which comes through frequency interference, explains how most birds can produce specific vibratos thanks to their unique throat and larynx anatomy. This phenomenon is also a specific vocal technique in Persian and Azeri music called Tahrir, where the singer imitates the same sound by phases of blocking the vocal cords to create a falsetto appoggiatura in different intervals before the main tone.

In this artistic approach, a vocal ensemble with four singers experienced the same phenomenon by singing while a transducer, which plays a sine wave with a slight pitch difference, made contact with their throats.

Performing Details

  • Although the text is in Persian, the score is written in IPA (International Phonetic Alphabet) characters and requires accurate pronunciation.

Text:

به تصویر درختی
که در حوض
زیر یخ زندانیست،
چه بگویم؟
(بیژن الهی)

/be/ /tæsvi:re/ /deræxti:/ /ke/ /dær/ /hoʊz/ /zi:re/ /jæx/ /zendani:st/ /t͡ʃe/ /begu:jæm/

To the Tree’s Image
    In the Pond
        Captured Beneath the Ice,
How Shall I Converse?
(Bijan Elahi, 1945–2010)

In the Score:

  • Symbols are accurately chosen from meaningful musical symbols and IPA characters.
  • Green lines and symbols represent notes for vocalists.
  • Pink lines represent sine waves produced by transducers.

Equipment: Wearable transducers (such as a necklace) should directly touch the bones of the throat. A slight pitch difference (a few Hertz) will create physical beating, which resonates in the mouth of the singer.

Equipment was provided with the generous support of the Aksenov Family Foundation for the NOMADISM project at The VOICES Performing Arts Festival, November 16, 2024, RadialSystem Berlin. Premiered by PHØNIX16.

Electronics: A Half-Dom ambisonic system is required to play the electronic part. The venue was equipped by L-ACOUSTICS using L-ISA software for spatialization.

Singers will be guided and tuned using a click track, alongside a 2-second crescendo at the starting frequency.

Choreography

An abstract choreography for one dancer, who moves from one side of the stage and disappears on the other side. Three levels of speed apply:

  • Fastest: Head movement — looking at the audience, then looking away.
  • Medium: Leg movement — incorporating backward movement.
  • Slow: Hand movement — starting wide and open, culminating in a self-embrace.

Video

Prototype and documentation recording.

  • 00:00 – 01:40 — Prototype demonstrating voice manipulation with transducers
  • 01:46 – 01:58 — Short example of how it sounded in performance
  • 02:04 – 02:36 — Short example of the dancer’s performance
  • 02:42 – end — Short example of what the full performance looked like

TEXNO

Read from 4:22 to 6:53 of the piece.

Entity is a portion of every potential input & output,
where each portion equals one,
and it could be something or a Ding*.

All the inputs that are given to one as a chain of forces,
through which no-one is able to make any choice at the beginning,
therefore these inputs that are given to a Ding at the beginning,
and it remains the same until the end is considered as one’s identity.

Although each output is related to one or more inputs in the past,
no-one remains exactly the same as the beginning,
therefore there is a reason for this question to be asked:
Is there any territory in one’s entity dedicated to a Ding that is Not-Identity?

How are the meanings given in the last minute being processed?

At the same territory as a given question is being asked,
there is a questioner’s mind that is a portion of an entity
but it is not identity
and also Es** is neither follower nor influencer of the identity,
so Es is neuter and deep in the Ding’s subconsciousness.

Through its communication with identity an answer to a need been created,
which is sharing with sounds in order to communicate with oneself,
whether one with a Ding as itself or with any others.

Also Es as a Ding,
which is being shared in communication with the identity, is learnable.
So, Es is knowledge given to one.

Since it doesn’t remain the same from the beginning until the end,
and it comes through conversation
so it’s not an identity
not even entity
but it’s been assumed by both
as it was conversed with the identity
by the one’s Esentity***.

Samir TimajChi, Nov. 2024

* “Ding” in German can be translated as “thing” in English, but philosophically, “Ding” refers to a being that is independent of its function.
** “Es” in German can be translated as “it” in English.
*** “Esentity” : “Itentity”

entry.title: (infinite)
entry.content:
Abstract

(infinite) approaches a de-conceptualization of music into free-form sounds independent of time and space. The central concept is the absence of dictatorship and hierarchies of sound. The composer is a mere facilitator; true authorship lies with human-machine assemblages exploring random processing and self-organized structures. Algorithmic randomness serves as a complementary method examining sound from non-human-biased perspectives.

Research Questions

  • How does musical composition incorporate rhizomatic movements by working with a non-hierarchical form structured to have an independent large-scale structure?
  • How does the machine display its agency?

Method

A Bösendorfer Imperial Piano on stage, surrounded by nine microphones and a camera mounted above. A performer in a green suit (chroma key) recorded 3,000+ individual audio and visual recordings using vibrators, screwdrivers, steel balls, ventilators, table tennis balls, and extended piano techniques.

Files are systematically named with parameters (duration, pitch, sound family, average amplitude, position, etc.) stored in a database. Audiences can interact by altering parameters and solving puzzles hidden for discovery.

Structure — The Rhizome

Musical material is algorithmically combined. Performance structure mimics rhizome growth: dominant stolons branch out, generating new stolons indefinitely. A stolon can be defined by mode of production, set of strings, loudness, length, or number of performers. Up to ten stolons active simultaneously. Other sound events group randomly around a stolon until one establishes a new stolon — self-replication with variation. Rate of change is driven by a random number generator following patterns.

Results are displayed on a website performing the instrument in real time, with each client receiving fresh output at any moment.

Technology

Technical stack: WebAudio API, Three.js, custom database, WebGL, QR code system.

Interaction design: passive autonomous state (1–10 layers) → user unlocks deeper layers via clicks/QR codes → each visit generates a unique performance.

Recorded at the Hybrid New Music Lab, Hochschule für Musik Carl Maria von Weber Dresden.

Rethinking Technology-Based Music

The choice of Max/MSP, Pure Data, and p5.js as focal tools is predicated on their distinguished positions within the computer music community. Max/MSP — developed at IRCAM in the late 1980s by Miller Puckette and later commercialized by Cycling ‘74 — resonates with Umberto Eco’s concept of the “open work”: art open to multiple interpretations, aligning with Stockhausen’s Klavierstücke XI.

These environments function as “distributed labs” rather than mere software tools — global collaborative spaces for experimentation, aligned with GNU/Linux licensing principles.

The following recordings document three phases of the system’s development:

entry.title: The Art of Virtuoso
entry.content:
Concept

Dedicated to Forgotten Sounds

Have you ever noticed those tiny, almost inaudible sounds during a concert? These sounds could represent voices that are hidden in the crowd and gradually forgotten.

As someone without a background in classical music, I was never fascinated by the complex vertical and horizontal relationships in music, which were literally unrecognizable through listening alone. I also never understood the purpose of a virtuoso performer’s extra movements.

However, in my mind, I could imagine sounds that weren’t necessarily audible but still existed. I found myself immersed in the imagination of these sounds and felt a connection to them. This experience marked the beginning of my sympathy for these forgotten sounds.

Structure

Three performers (wind instrument + keyboard + string instrument) interpret a score richly layered with Classical Music fragments. These fragments are interspersed throughout, with performers using virtuosic expressive gestures mirroring the emotional depth of the classical compositions.

EMG sensors on performers’ arms capture muscle tension data, processed in Max/MSP to simulate original fragments on an event-based patch. The piece also includes analog sounds of sleeve rubbing against the body and collar rubbing against the neck, captured through piezoelectric/contact microphones.

Performers’ heartbeats and breathing are amplified using wearable devices. The performance culminates in a serene finale where amplified heartbeats and breathing are presented in compositional fragmentation.

Technical Implementation

EMG System

A music control system using an EMG (Electromyography) sensor and Arduino UNO. Three electrodes attach to the arm; the EMG sensor reads muscle electrical signals; Arduino converts them to digital data; Max/MSP turns the signals into sound.

Hardware: EMG sensor (~€15), Arduino UNO (~€25), 2× 9V batteries (~€5) — total under €50.

Arduino code:

int sensorPin = A0;
int sensorValue = 0;
void setup() {
    pinMode(sensorPin, INPUT);
    Serial.begin(9600);
}
void loop() {
    sensorValue = analogRead(sensorPin);
    Serial.println(sensorValue);
    delay(5);
}

Signal latency: ~5 ms total.

Max/MSP Patch

Signal flow: serial input (9600 baud) → scale 0–1 + smoothing → split into control ranges → map to frequency/amplitude. Strong contractions (>800) trigger lower frequencies; weaker movements control higher tones.

Body Locations

Video

Samir TimajChi — 30 November 2024
entry.summary: For Trio with EMG sensors, contact microphones, and Max/MSP.

entry.title: Hung Hair
entry.content:
Concept

Hung Hair delves into the often overlooked executions led by the standing and battling for Women’s Rights — as well as the shooting of people on the streets — and all about fighting for the freedom of dress, a right suppressed by compulsory rules imposed by governments in countries such as the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan and Iran, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia, Chechnya, and others.

The work relates to the exploitative point of view of the human from government, applied to part or all of society. What is happening in these lands has nothing to do with hypothetical texts on papers — it is a loud yell and a bloody fight.

Structure

  1. The performer is hung from their feet.
  2. On the floor a canvas is placed, under which several piezoelectric sensors (microphones) are mounted to capture data that will be manipulated and transformed into sounds.
  3. A washable bucket of paint the same color as the canvas — preferably canvas, costume, makeup, and painting all in white.
  4. Dramaturgy of lights.

How to Perform

The hanging performer will start painting with their hair as a paintbrush. At the end, they cut their hair and spread it on the canvas, then imitate the electronic sounds created by touching the canvas.

Work in Progress — July 2023
Samir TimajChi
entry.summary: Performance work exploring executions, women's rights, and the fight for freedom of dress.
